message.content:
Here’s a quick‑reference guide you can keep handy (or print out) so your piano stays happy and healthy:

| # | Tip | Why it matters |
|---|-----|----------------|
| **1** | **Control Humidity & Temperature** | Pianos expand/contract with moisture changes. Aim for ~45–55 % relative humidity and keep the room between 65–75°F (18–24°C). Use a hygrometer + humidifier/dehumidifier as needed. |
| **2** | **Keep It Clean – but Don’t Overdo It** | Dust daily with a soft microfiber cloth; avoid harsh chemicals or water on keys, pedals, or inside the case. For deeper cleanings, use a damp rag only on surfaces—never let liquid seep into cracks. |
| **3** | **Regular Tuning** | A professional tuner should tune an acoustic piano at least twice a year (more often if heavily used). Digital pianos don’t require this, but check pitch stability regularly. |
| **4** | **Check Pedals & Action** | Inspect pedal cables and springs monthly. If pedals feel sluggish or sticky, have them serviced. Lightly oil action components (if recommended by manufacturer) once a year. |
| **5** | **Avoid Extreme Sunlight / Direct Heat Sources** | UV light fades finish; direct heat dries wood. Keep the piano away from radiators, vents, or windows where sunlight hits directly for long periods. |
| **6** | **Use Proper Footwear Inside the Piano Room** | Shoes with hard soles can damage the floor beneath the piano. Consider a dedicated “piano area” rug or mat. |
| **7** | **Move With Care** | When relocating, always use a piano dolly and lift both ends of the lid. Never tip over or place heavy objects on top of the piano. |
| **8** | **Inspect Strings & Hammers Regularly** | Look for broken strings, loose pins, or worn hammers. Replace damaged parts promptly to prevent further wear. |
| **9** | **Maintain the Finish** | Polish the exterior with a mild furniture polish no more than once per month. Avoid waxes that may attract dust. |
| **10** | **Professional Servicing** | Every few years, bring the piano in for a full service: inspection, lubrication, adjustment of escapement, and checking internal mechanisms. |

### Quick Checklist (Every Month)

- [ ] Check humidity level  
- [ ] Wipe down keys & surface  
- [ ] Test pedal response  
- [ ] Listen for odd sounds during play  

### Quick Checklist (Quarterly)

- [ ] Deep clean interior (with help of a pro if unsure)  
- [ ] Lubricate moving parts (as per manual)  
- [ ] Verify structural integrity (no visible cracks)  

By following these simple habits, you'll preserve tone quality, extend lifespan, and enjoy playing without unexpected surprises!
